newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share market sags on poor sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share market sags on poor sentiment.

text.p: The Singapore stock market closed lower on Thursday in weak sentiment, dealers said.
"Sentiment is pretty poor. Looking at both micro and macro factors, investors are not expecting any good news from Singapore," a dealer said.
Dealers expected the market to stay range-bound.
"Whenever there is a sell-off in blue-chips, they become good bargains again," the dealer said. "So this market should see range-trading."
The Straits Times Industrials Index closed 24.89 points or 1.17 percent lower at 2,110.57.
Market volume was light at 89.1 million shares, with crossed trades comprising the bulk of the deals. Losers led gainers at 249 to 88.

Jurong Cement and Malaysian counter Rashid Hussain were among gainers, rising S$0.15 (US$0.11) each to S$5.75 and S$8.35 respectively. Cerebos Pacific and Singapore Press Foreign fell S$0.40 to S$10.90 and S$23.60 respectively.
Malaysian Causeway Invest topped the actives with 15.9 million shares, including about 9.8 million shares crossed.
Dealers said upside on Malaysian counters was capped by talk of fund sales.
